source.title: Abdulla Rexhepi and Zeqije Xhafce, Exploring Hurufi-Bektashi Sufism in Albanian Literature. Insights from an Old Manuscript
evidence_lines_seen: Article frames the object as a Hurufi-Bektashi manuscript and as a junk / Turkish conk.
The manuscript is reported as 135 pages: 90 pages Albanian and the remaining pages Turkish and Persian.
The Turkish/Persian author roster includes Nesimi, Yunus Emre, Kizil Deli Dede, Esrefoglu, Hakiki and Hatai.
The manuscript is reported in Millet Library, Ali Emiri collection, Istanbul; old registration no. 551 and new no. 003094.

new_or_reinforced_leads.why_it_matters: This is the first new open-web Balkan Hurufi-Bektashi physical manuscript lead surfaced in this continuation. It is not derivative of the Diyarbakir/Ilkhchi Sohrabiabad-Akin article and it co-locates Hakiki with Hatai and Nesimi in a Bektashi-Hurufi manuscript context.
risk_and_disambiguation: No Hakiki incipit, folio, image, explicit, or item count is published.
Hakiki may be Cihan Shah, Yusuf Hakiki, Agazade Mehmed Dede, a local Bektashi/Hurufi namesake, or a simplified author-roster label.
The article proves Bektashi-Hurufi manuscript context, not current Alevi cem use.
The Millet/Ali Emiri catalogue record must be resolved directly before promotion.

false_positive_classes_reinforced.description: Full-corpus grep produces many hakikat/hakiki adjective hits that are not a poet name.
Hakiki Makam is a real Ehl-i Hak ritual/music term; useful for route terminology but not a Hakiki author signal by itself.
Ilahi mecmuas can contain Hakiki poems from non-Jahanshah Ottoman religious poets. The 06 Mil Yz A 7978 case is a probable example, pending direct incipit capture.

The only new live desk lead came from the Balkan Hurufi-Bektashi manuscript route, not from Turkish institutional catalogue title search.
